title: Auditor access models across Ethereum, Canton, Corda, and Rayls Enygma Public
research_question: How can financial institutions make private transactions on a public blockchain while retaining auditability and institutional control?

scope.focus: Who can read transaction data, what permission or mechanism provides access, and what the access boundary is.
exclusions: This record does not prove the configuration of a specific production Canton or Corda network.
This record does not independently decrypt an Enygma account's escrowed view key or verify the current testnet auditor account.
This record does not establish that all auditors have equivalent rights across the four systems.

sources.title: Networks
sources.version_or_scope: Ethereum public networks; page describes public network access generally and identifies Ethereum Mainnet as the primary production network.
relevant_evidence: Public networks are accessible to anyone with an internet connection.
Anyone can read or create transactions on a public blockchain and validate transactions.
does_not_support: A separate auditor role or auditor-specific permission system at Ethereum base layer.
The proposition that all information in every privacy-enabled Ethereum application is publicly readable.

sources.title: Local and external parties
relevant_evidence: An Observing Participant Node (OPN) has observation permissions for a hosted party.
The party entrusts its OPNs to record and provide read access to transactions involving that party.
A node with only observation permissions cannot submit or confirm transactions on behalf of the hosted party.
supports: Canton read-only observation permission scoped to a hosted party
does_not_support: A network-wide auditor with visibility into all Canton transactions.
Automatic access for a regulator that has not been granted the relevant party/participant relationship.

sources.title: Topology management
relevant_evidence: Observation permission means the participant node is notified only of transactions in which the hosted party is a stakeholder.
Confirmation permission includes observation; submission permission includes confirmation.
supports: Canton observation access is party-scoped and assigned through hosting topology
does_not_support: An auditor can inspect transactions unrelated to the party whose activity is observed.
Observation permission is globally read-only in every possible operational configuration beyond the documented permission semantics.

sources.title: Glossary of concepts
relevant_evidence: A contract observer is a party on a contract that can see that contract instance and its information.
Participant nodes maintain a private contract store containing contracts the participant is privy to; there is no global contract store.
Sub-transaction privacy means participants learn only the subset of a transaction in which they are directly involved.
supports: Canton contract-level observer semantics and participant-specific data visibility
does_not_support: A general-purpose regulatory auditor automatically sees every contract in a network.

sources.title: Posting transactions to observer nodes
sources.version_or_scope: Corda Enterprise 4.10 tutorial; do not silently generalize implementation details to all Corda versions.
relevant_evidence: R3 describes observer nodes as a common finance requirement where regulators want reporting on actions taken.
A regulator can run its own node and receive digitally signed, deduplicated reports.
The tutorial's application flow explicitly sends a signed transaction to a regulator and records it using ALL_VISIBLE.
supports: Corda Enterprise 4.10 application-integrated observer-node reporting to regulators
does_not_support: A Corda-wide auditor identity with automatic access to every transaction.
The assertion that every Corda application sends every transaction to every regulator by default.

sources.title: Who sees what in Enygma Public
relevant_evidence: The deployment auditor can read each shielded transaction, including sender, recipient, amount, and token.
At account registration, the wallet encrypts a copy of the view key to the deployment auditor key using ML-KEM-768 and stores it in the registry.
The auditor's view uses that key to open account view keys and display shielded transactions.
The view key does not provide spend authority; spending requires the account spend key.
The documentation says no Enygma Public contract can freeze, pause, or block funds, while also noting that the owner multisig can upgrade registry or shared-vault rules.
The page states that the Rayls team is the auditor on testnet.
supports: Enygma Public's documented deployment-level auditor mechanism
Read/decrypt capability separated from spend capability
Testnet auditor identity as an official documentation claim
does_not_support: Independent proof that the current testnet auditor actually decrypted a specific account or transaction during this review.
An immutable guarantee that freeze-related behavior can never change, because owner-multisig upgrades can change relevant contract rules.

sources.title: Enygma Public
relevant_evidence: The product is live on Rayls Public Chain testnet and uses test tokens with no value.
The deployment auditor can read shielded payments.
One auditor key is associated with each deployment; the page describes a deployment boundary, such as a country-level deployment.
The owner multisig can upgrade the registry and shared vault, register vaults, and add verifying keys.
does_not_support: Historical testnet configuration at every prior block without historical state or deployment evidence.

sources.title: How Enygma Public works
relevant_evidence: The account's view key is an ML-KEM-768 key pair.
The wallet encrypts a copy of the view key to the deployment auditor key during registration.
The account's notes are readable by the owner and auditor, while the spend key remains necessary to spend notes.
supports: Technical explanation of view-key escrow and separation of read and spend authority
does_not_support: Independent cryptographic verification of the testnet auditor's private key custody or successful decryption.

ethereum.auditor_access_model: Public read access to public-chain data; no separate auditor-only access boundary is documented at the base network layer.
ethereum.caveat: Applications and privacy layers may keep application data or plaintext outside public ledger visibility.

canton.auditor_access_model: Party-scoped observation permission for participant nodes and contract-level observer rights in Daml.
canton.scope: Transactions/contracts in which the hosted party is a stakeholder or observer.
canton.caveat: Do not label this a universal network-wide auditor. Access depends on party hosting permissions, contract stakeholders, and application design.

corda.auditor_access_model: Application-integrated observer node; regulator node receives transactions explicitly reported by application flows.
corda.scope: Transactions sent to the observer through the CorDapp flow and the visibility/recording options used.
corda.caveat: The cited observer tutorial is Corda Enterprise 4.10. It is not proof that every Corda version or CorDapp automatically reports every transaction.

rayls_enygma_public.auditor_access_model: Deployment auditor key used to decrypt escrowed account view keys.
rayls_enygma_public.scope: Every shielded transaction within the auditor's own deployment, according to current official product documentation.
rayls_enygma_public.caveat: A specific live decryption was not independently tested. Relevant contract rules are upgradeable by the owner multisig.

corrected_comparison_table.concise_claim: Public read access to on-chain data
corrected_comparison_table.auditor_access: Anyone can read public ledger data; no auditor-specific role at base layer is evidenced here.
OPN and Daml observers see only transactions/contracts within granted party or contract visibility.
Regulator node receives signed transactions explicitly reported by application flow.
Auditor key opens escrowed account view keys to read shielded transactions in that deployment.

limitations_and_open_questions: Canton and Corda are permissioned deployments. Public documentation proves described capabilities, not the configuration of a named bank, regulator, or production network.
The cited Corda observer evidence is version-specific to Enterprise 4.10; compatibility with Corda 5.x requires a separate version-specific source review.
Canton OPN access is party-scoped and should not be conflated with Daml contract observer rights; they operate at related but distinct layers.
Enygma documentation describes a deployment auditor key and escrow model, but no independent testnet decryption was performed in this review.
The fact that a view key cannot spend funds does not by itself prove that the auditor cannot correlate other public metadata or that governance rules cannot change.
The terminal runtime network request failed due DNS resolution, so no command-line retrieval or cryptographic hash verification of the live source pages is claimed.
